Description: Always animate GPU-accelerated properties (x, y, scale, rotate, opacity) instead of layout properties (width, height, top, left, margin).
Do: Use x y scale opacity for smooth 60/120fps animations
Don't: Animate width height top left or padding which trigger layout reflow
Code Good: <motion.div initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 16 }} animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} transition={{ duration: 0.3 }} />

Description: Wrap conditional components in AnimatePresence with mode="wait" or mode="popLayout" to animate removal from DOM.
Do: Always provide a unique key on immediate children of AnimatePresence
Don't: Forget key prop or put AnimatePresence inside the conditional branch
Code Good: <AnimatePresence mode="wait">{isVisible && (<motion.div key="modal" initial={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 }} animate={{ opacity: 1, scale: 1 }} exit={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.95 }} />)}</AnimatePresence>

Guideline: Use variants for orchestrated and clean animation states
Description: Define animation variants outside component to keep JSX clean and orchestrate staggered children automatically.
Do: Use variants with staggerChildren and delayChildren for list/card reveals
Don't: Inline massive animate objects inside every JSX tag
Code Good: const container = { hidden: { opacity: 0 }, show: { opacity: 1, transition: { staggerChildren: 0.08 } } }; const item = { hidden: { opacity: 0, y: 12 }, show: { opacity: 1, y: 0 } }; return (<motion.ul variants={container} initial="hidden" animate="show">{items.map(i => <motion.li key={i.id} variants={item} />)}</motion.ul>);
Code Bad: <motion.div animate={{ opacity: 1, y: 0, transition: { duration: 0.4, delay: index * 0.1 } }} />

Guideline: Use layout prop for automatic UI reflow transitions
Description: Add layout prop to elements whose position/size changes when siblings expand, filter, or reorder.
Do: Use layout with spring transition for smooth accordion and grid reflow
Don't: Manually calculate element bounding boxes and tween heights

Guideline: Use layoutId for seamless morphing transitions
Description: Share a layoutId between two components across different views or tabs to smoothly morph from one into the other (e.g. active tab indicator or card expansion).
Do: Set layoutId on active pill/indicator or card-to-modal expander
Code Good: {isActive && <motion.div layoutId="active-indicator" className="absolute inset-0 bg-primary rounded-full" transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 380, damping: 30 }} />}

Guideline: Use whileHover and whileTap for interactive micro-feedback
Description: Add whileHover, whileTap, and whileFocus for spring-driven, interruptible micro-interactions on buttons, cards, and links.
Do: Combine whileHover={{ y: -2, scale: 1.02 }} with whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }} and cursor-pointer
Don't: Rely on brittle CSS :hover transitions without tap/active feedback
Code Good: <motion.button whileHover={{ scale: 1.02, y: -2 }} whileTap={{ scale: 0.98 }} transition={{ type: "spring", stiffness: 400, damping: 17 }} className="cursor-pointer">Click Me</motion.button>

Guideline: Use whileInView for lazy viewport entrance animations
Description: Animate elements as they scroll into view using whileInView and viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-50px" }}.
Do: Set once: true for standard reveals so scrolling up and down does not re-trigger jarring entrance animations
Don't: Attach scroll listeners to window and measure element offsetTop manually
Code Good: <motion.section initial={{ opacity: 0, y: 24 }} whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }} viewport={{ once: true, margin: "-100px" }} transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeOut" }} />

Guideline: Use useScroll and useTransform for parallax and reading progress
Description: Link scroll progress to styles declaratively using useScroll and useTransform hooks without performance bottlenecks.
Do: Use scrollYProgress with useTransform for parallax header and progress bar
Don't: Update React state inside scroll handler causing 60 rerenders per second
Code Good: const { scrollYProgress } = useScroll({ target: containerRef, offset: ["start end", "end start"] }); const y = useTransform(scrollYProgress, [0, 1], [-50, 50]); return <motion.div style={{ y }} />;

Description: Respect user accessibility preferences by checking useReducedMotion and disabling displacement/scaling.
Do: Fallback to instant switch or subtle opacity fade when reduced motion is requested
Don't: Force high-velocity movement and scale bounces on users with vestibular disorders
Code Good: const shouldReduce = useReducedMotion(); const variants = { hidden: { opacity: 0, y: shouldReduce ? 0 : 20 }, show: { opacity: 1, y: 0 } };

Guideline: Tune spring physics with stiffness and damping
Description: Use spring transitions instead of duration/easing for natural, organic motion that adapts gracefully to rapid user clicks.
Do: Use stiffness: 300, damping: 25 for standard UI; stiffness: 400, damping: 15 for bouncy accents
Don't: Use linear or harsh duration easing for interactive gestures

Guideline: Animate SVG pathLength for outline drawing effects
Description: Create drawing effects on icons, illustrations, and checkmarks using pathLength and pathOffset.
Do: Use pathLength: 1 with spring or easeInOut for checkmarks and icons
Code Good: <motion.path d="M5 13l4 4L19 7" initial={{ pathLength: 0 }} animate={{ pathLength: 1 }} transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: "easeInOut" }} />

Guideline: Implement drag gestures with constraints and snapping
Description: Use drag, dragConstraints, and dragElastic to build carousels, bottom sheets, sliders, and dismissible cards.
Do: Provide dragConstraints with ref or coordinate box, and handle onDragEnd for threshold dismissal
Don't: Attach custom mousemove/touchmove handlers and calculate client coordinates
Code Good: <motion.div drag="x" dragConstraints={{ left: -100, right: 100 }} dragElastic={0.2} onDragEnd={(e, { offset }) => { if (offset.x > 80) handleDismiss(); }} />
